sources.entry: ejabberd - XMPP instant messaging server. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 Erlang/Docker
ejabberd | Robust, scalable XMPP, MQTT and SIP server

summary.one_liner: ejabberd is an open-source, scalable realtime server built on Erlang/OTP that provides an XMPP server, MQTT broker, and SIP service.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes ejabberd as a robust, scalable, and extensible realtime platform built with Erlang/OTP, including an XMPP server, an MQTT broker, and a SIP service. It can be installed from source (compiled with ./configure and make), from ProcessOne installers or GitHub Releases, from Docker container images (an "ecs" image for x64 and an "ejabberd" image for x64 and arm64), from OS packages, or via Homebrew. After installation, the README points to the ejabberdctl command and the ejabberd.yml man page for configuration help. Bug reports go to GitHub Issues, translations go through Weblate, and nightly builds are available from GitHub Actions and GitHub Packages. The README links to external docs for features, supported XEPs, and developer material rather than documenting them inline.
use_cases: run a self-hosted XMPP chat server
deploy a scalable instant messaging backend
run a chat server in Docker
set up a team or community messaging server
how_to_run: Install from a ProcessOne installer or GitHub Releases package, or from your OS package manager or Homebrew
Or pull a Docker image: the ejabberd container image from GitHub Packages (x64 and arm64), or the ecs image from Docker Hub (x64)
Or compile from source: ./configure and make (run ./configure --help and make help for options)
After installation, run ejabberdctl help for commands
See man ejabberd.yml for configuration reference
notable: Combines XMPP server, MQTT broker, and SIP service in one Erlang/OTP platform
Multiple install routes: source, installers, Docker images, OS packages, Homebrew
Nightly builds available for master branch and pull requests
Supports the XMPP extensions listed on the ProcessOne and XMPP.org pages
caveats: Commercial support, the Business Edition, and the Fluux cloud offering are provided by ProcessOne and are separate from the open-source project
The ecs Docker image is x64 only
